newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to boost 1-yr bond offer as demand grows.
newsitem.headline: Poland to boost 1-yr bond offer as demand grows.

text.p: Poland will boost its offer of one-year index linked bonds to meet large public demand stirred up by attractive discounts, a senior finance ministry official said on Wednesday.

"Taking into account large retail demand the finance minstry decided to issue 900 million zloty of one-year bonds in June against the March 400 million zloty offer," Piotr Dziewulski, head of the ministry's public debt department told a news conference.

Dziewulski said that attractive pricing at 96.50 of the par value allowed to keep demand from sagging even though from the start of this year investments in government securities were no longer tax deductible.
He said individual investors have already bought all 207.9 million zlotys worth of the bonds offered to the general public from March 3 at an issue price of 96.50.
"A planned three-month offer was sold out in two weeks, which means investors found the paper attractive...despite a lack of tax deduction," Dziewulski said.
During an earlier subscription in which investors could buy bonds to roll-over earlier purchases 192.1 million zlotys worth of the bonds were sold at 95.50.

Dziewulski said that in order to prop up sales of floating-rate three-year bonds the ministry planned to use the same technique as with the one-year paper by offering the paper in separate, differently priced public and institutional tranches.

The ministry also announced it was issuing a total of four billion zlotys of new one-year bonds in four tranches of 900 million zlotys due June 4, 1998, 900 million due September 3, 1998, 1.1 billion maturing on December 3, 1998 and 1.1 billion maturing on March 4, 1999.
